sections.title: Advanced Concept of Coding-Decoding
sections.content: At Level 3, Coding-Decoding questions are complex and involve multiple logical operations. Two or three rules may be applied in sequence such as shifting letters, applying mathematical operations to positions, rearranging letters, and adding symbols or numbers. Careful observation and structured analysis are essential.

sections.title: Multi-Step Operation Pattern
sections.content: A word may undergo several steps. Step 1: Convert letters into their alphabet positions. Step 2: Apply mathematical operations like +3, -2, ×2, or square. Step 3: Convert the new numbers back into letters. Missing any step can lead to a wrong answer.

sections.title: Cyclic Alphabet Logic
sections.content: In cyclic patterns, counting continues from A after Z. For example, Y +3 becomes B. This pattern is common in higher-level shifting questions.

sections.title: Position-Based Rearrangement
sections.content: Letters may be rearranged in a fixed position pattern like 1-4-2-5-3 or 3-1-4-2. Identifying this positional mapping is crucial before applying other operations.

sections.title: Matrix or Grid Coding
sections.content: Some questions arrange letters in a grid and assign codes based on row and column numbers. For example, a letter in row 2 column 3 may be coded as 23.

sections.title: Number-Symbol Integration
sections.content: Words may be converted into numbers using sum, product, or difference of letter positions, and then combined with symbols. Example: Total sum of positions followed by a special character.

sections.title: Complex Sentence Coding
sections.content: Multiple sentences with overlapping words are given. Logical elimination is used to match each word with its correct code. Often distractor options are provided to confuse the candidate.

sections.title: Advanced Strategies
sections.content: 1. Break the pattern into clear steps. 2. Verify the rule using at least two letters. 3. Check for cyclic shifts. 4. Analyze positional rearrangement before shifting. 5. Use option elimination wisely.

sections.title: Common Errors
sections.content: 1. Ignoring cyclic continuation after Z. 2. Missing one step in multi-step coding. 3. Calculation mistakes in position values. 4. Assuming a simple pattern without full verification.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 3 Coding-Decoding includes multi-step operations, cyclic shifts, position rearrangement, grid-based logic, and mixed number-symbol coding. Success depends on systematic breakdown and logical verification.

tricks.title: Stepwise Decomposition Trick
tricks.explanation: Divide the coding process into separate steps and test each step independently.
tricks.example: First apply +2, then reverse, then subtract 1.

tricks.title: Cyclic Shift Check
tricks.explanation: If shifting crosses Z, continue counting from A.

tricks.title: Square Position Method
tricks.explanation: Check whether letter positions are squared before conversion.
tricks.example: D = 4, square is 16, which is P.

tricks.title: Alternate Multiply Rule
tricks.explanation: Odd position letters may be multiplied by 2 and even positions by 3.

tricks.title: Rearrangement Mapping Trick
tricks.explanation: Write position numbers below letters to detect rearrangement patterns.

tricks.title: Grid Visualization Method
tricks.explanation: Arrange alphabets in a 5x5 grid and check row-column logic.
tricks.example: Letter in row 3 column 2 coded as 32.

tricks.title: Difference Chain Analysis
tricks.explanation: Find the pattern of differences between consecutive letters.

tricks.title: Common Word Fixing Strategy
tricks.explanation: In sentence coding, lock the most repeated word first.
tricks.example: If a word appears three times with the same code, fix that mapping first.

tricks.title: Reverse Plus Shift Combo
tricks.explanation: Try reversing the word before applying shifting operations.

tricks.title: Advanced Option Elimination
tricks.explanation: Remove options that fail even one step of the identified rule.
tricks.example: If cyclic shift is involved, eliminate non-cyclic results.
